steps.text: Since the sizes are yours to set, I'll use the segmented print-in-place version and pick common defaults. I'll plan it first, since moving pieces need a plan before the sheet.

assumptions: Printed in PLA, since that is the loaded filament; PLA is stiff, so the joints move but the body does not flex.
Gap of 0.4 mm side to side and above and below, for the 0.4 mm nozzle in PLA.
Common defaults: 10 segments, 18 mm pitch, 20 mm height, tapering from 22 mm to 8 mm width.
Head is a simple wedge, with no sculpted detail.
questions: Should the flexi version be printed later in TPU, which needs the spool and a direct-drive print?

**How do you want to go on?** I can rebuild the chain with separate pin and socket steps so the plan matches, or keep it as built and accept that the plan check does not match. I have not sliced or sent anything to the printer.

The tail tip is a separate step I can add now. I'll build it on the tail end of segment 1 and fuse it there.

To pass, I would have to rebuild the chain with the pins and sockets as their own steps. That is about 20 more build calls. Should I do the rebuild, or accept the chain as built with the plan left failing? I have not sliced or sent anything to the printer.
